_note: FICTIONAL sample rubric for the bundled examples. Copy rubric_template.json for your own roles.

competencies.name: Reconciliation & accuracy
competencies.definition: Finds, explains and resolves differences between ledgers, bank data and subledgers, and prevents repeats.

anchors.1: Describes reconciliations only in general terms; cannot explain how a specific difference was found or resolved.
anchors.2: Walks through a reconciliation they ran, but relied on others to investigate differences or did not follow up on root cause.
anchors.3: Gives a specific example of finding, explaining and clearing a difference, with the checks they used and the outcome.
anchors.4: As 3, and changed a process or control so the same class of difference stopped recurring, with a measurable result.

competencies.name: Month-end close ownership
competencies.definition: Plans and delivers their part of the close on time, tracks dependencies and escalates early.

anchors.1: No example of owning close tasks or deadlines.
anchors.2: Completed assigned close tasks; little evidence of planning ahead or managing dependencies.
anchors.3: Owned a defined part of the close end to end, kept a checklist or calendar, and escalated a risk before it slipped.
anchors.4: Shortened or de-risked the close for the team (e.g. moved work earlier, automated a step) and can say by how much.

competencies.name: Systems & spreadsheet fluency
competencies.definition: Uses the ERP, bank exports and spreadsheets accurately, and builds work others can check and reuse.

anchors.1: Cannot describe how they built or checked a working file or report.
anchors.2: Uses standard functions and exports with guidance; files are hard for others to follow.
anchors.3: Builds clear, checkable workbooks or reports (lookups, pivots, tie-outs) and explains how they validate them.
anchors.4: Built a reusable tool, template or system integration that others adopted, with checks built in.

competencies.name: Stakeholder communication
competencies.definition: Explains finance issues clearly to non-finance colleagues and gets what is needed from them on time.

anchors.1: Examples show unclear requests or no follow-through with other teams.
anchors.2: Communicates when asked; relies on the manager to chase or explain to other teams.
anchors.3: Gives an example of explaining a finance issue to a non-finance colleague and agreeing a next step that happened.
anchors.4: As 3, and changed how another team works with finance (e.g. a new intake form or SLA) with a visible result.

competencies.name: Process improvement
competencies.definition: Spots manual or error-prone steps and improves them, measuring the effect.

anchors.1: No example of improving a process.
anchors.2: Suggested an improvement but did not implement it or measure it.
anchors.3: Implemented an improvement to a finance process and can describe the before and after.
anchors.4: Led an improvement across teams or systems with a measured saving in time or errors.

competencies.name: Collaboration & feedback
competencies.definition: Shares work openly, asks for and acts on feedback, and helps teammates hit shared deadlines.

anchors.1: Examples show working in isolation or dismissing feedback.
anchors.2: Accepts feedback when given; few examples of helping others.
anchors.3: Gives a specific example of asking for feedback, acting on it, and helping a teammate meet a deadline.
anchors.4: As 3, and set up a habit or practice that improved how the team shares work or feedback.

questions.text: Tell me about a reconciliation difference you found that took real digging. How did you find the cause?
What did you change afterwards so it didn't happen again?
Describe a time you had to explain a finance problem to someone outside finance. What happened next?
Tell me about feedback you got on your work and what you did with it.
Walk me through the part of the month-end close you owned. How did you keep it on track?
Show or describe a workbook or report you built. How would someone else check it?
Tell me about a time you helped a teammate hit a deadline.
Here is a bank-to-ledger tie-out that is off. Talk me through how you would find the difference.
How would you set this file up so next month's tie-out is faster?
Which manual step in this process would you remove first, and how would you know it worked?
